title: A CSV header named "name" comes back as "\ufeffname" and every lookup by column name fails
assumption: Decoding an uploaded CSV file as UTF-8 and reading its first header exactly recovers the column name the file's first line shows on screen.

input.description: A CSV saved from Excel with the "CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited)" format (and by many other Windows tools), which writes a UTF-8 byte-order mark at the very start of the file - invisible in a spreadsheet and in most text editors, but present as real bytes. (Excel's plain "CSV (Comma delimited)" format writes no BOM, and uses the system code page rather than UTF-8.)

what_goes_wrong: Decoding the file's bytes as plain `"utf-8"` leaves the BOM as a literal U+FEFF character glued onto the first header, so the first column parses as `"\ufeffname"` instead of `"name"` - a lookup like `row["name"]` throws a KeyError even though the column is clearly named "name" in every spreadsheet viewer.
why: A UTF-8 BOM is three specific bytes (EF BB BF) that some encoders prepend to mark a file as UTF-8; it decodes to the single code point U+FEFF. Decoding with Python's `"utf-8"` codec or Node's `Buffer.toString("utf8")` passes that code point through unchanged as the first character of the text. Python's `"utf-8-sig"` codec, and JavaScript's `TextDecoder("utf-8")` (whose spec-default `ignoreBOM: false` means the BOM *is* processed/stripped, despite the confusing name), both detect and strip a leading BOM - but only if you use them instead of the plain decoder.

repros.code:
raw = '\ufeffname,age\nAda,30\n'.encode("utf-8")
import csv, io
plain = raw.decode("utf-8")
sig = raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
print(list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(plain)))[0])
print(list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(sig)))[0])

fix: Decode uploaded CSV/text files with `encoding="utf-8-sig"` in Python (it strips a BOM if present and is a no-op if absent), or use `TextDecoder("utf-8")` (not a raw `Buffer.toString`) in Node, which strips the BOM by default. Alternatively, explicitly strip a leading `\ufeff` from the decoded text before parsing.

test_cases.note: A CSV-parsing function given text starting with a BOM character should strip it, so the header reads exactly "name" rather than "\ufeffname".
